explanation.headline: FDA's records trace our supply to a plant classified VAI 693 days before the shortage posting

sentences.text: Cytarabine is not on FDA's current shortage list as of 2026-10-21; FDA's history shows an earlier shortage first posted on 2021-09-24, since resolved.
FDA inspection 1110628 at Gland Pharma Limited ended 2019-11-01 and was classified VAI, with the classification letter dated 2019-12-10 — 693 days before FDA posted the shortage on 2021-09-24.
Gland Pharma Limited (FEI 3009056604) received VAI classifications in 2013, 2015, and 2019, and its most recent inspection was NAI on 2023-07-28.
Corvale East has 8.7 days of supply on hand for the 100 mg/mL, 20 mL presentation, while Corvale General has 24.5 days.

The top-ranked option is to transfer 16 vials of cytarabine 100 mg/mL, 20 mL from Corvale General to Corvale East, which would bring Corvale East to 14 days on hand while Corvale General retains 19 days.

rejected.text: The Corvale General and Corvale East inventory for cytarabine 100 mg/mL, 20 mL vials (NDC 25021022320) is labeled as manufactured by GLAND, which corresponds to Gland Pharma Limited.
rejected.reason: GLAND is named only as the application's sponsor, not as a manufacturing plant

memory.text: Decision on carboplatin: move the primary carboplatin contract from Accord to Teva and keep Accord as secondary. Rationale: Accord's supplier plant had an FDA warning letter; Teva supply steadier (demo history). Approved by Riley Brooks, PharmD.

Decision on carboplatin: restrict carboplatin to curative-intent regimens while on allocation; oncology reviews each palliative order. Rationale: Two suppliers on allocation and under 10 days on hand at Corvale General (demo history). Approved by Jordan Hale, PharmD.

Decision on lidocaine: switch lidocaine 1% 30 mL vials to 5 mL vials in the ED to reduce waste during the shortage. Rationale: Single-dose waste was a third of use (demo history). Approved by Alex Morgan, PharmD.
